scenes.setting: Derrick has learned to show rather than tell: with Mr. Fool's permission he conjures the expedition from memory above the bronze table — collapsed walls, ruined streets, the dark going on and on — and Klein watches, sighing at what the City of Silver endures
scenes.text_anchor: It's more attractive than any novel I've ever read

scenes.setting: The mural and then the statues, held on screen together: nobody at the table can name the six, Klein recognises them from the Tudor ruin as “Evernight, Sun, Storm, Wisdom, Earth, Giant” corrupted, Audrey finds her own Goddess among them and understands who disfigured Her, and Alger names it — the orthodox six, distorted, beside the Fallen Creator who did it

the table alone: Fors asks why there is no God of Steam and Machinery and learns He wasn't born until the late Fourth Epoch, then Derrick asks whether the mural is the key and thanks a Hanged Man nobody has ever called kind and enthusiastic
scenes.text_anchor: “Why is there no God of Steam and Machinery?”

scenes.setting: the table alone: the discussion over, Klein gives them the name the City of Silver found in the abandoned temple -- an organization of fallen angels -- and keeps the right to interpret it
